key_terms: Airflow's store for Dag Runs, task instances, scheduling state and configuration. A successful connection to it does not prove that output data still exists.
The scheduler's periodically updated liveness timestamp. A stale heartbeat reveals a stopped scheduler even when the API server returns HTTP 200.
The recorded status of one task in one Dag Run, such as queued, running, success, failed or up_for_retry.
The Docker volume that holds the workshop's metadata, logs, attempt markers and outputs so they survive replacing the container image or process.

worked_examples.title: Read component health instead of an HTTP status
worked_examples.code:
import json
import urllib.request

url = "http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v2/monitor/health"
with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=5) as response:
    data = json.loads(response.read(16_385))
components = ("metadatabase", "scheduler", "dag_processor", "triggerer")
print({name: data[name]["status"] for name in components})
worked_examples.interpretation: This mirrors the project health.py, which runs inside the Airflow container. A healthy deployment prints four entries, each with the status healthy. The endpoint can answer with HTTP 200 while the scheduler entry says unhealthy, because the API server is a separate process from the scheduler; a probe that stops at the status code would report a stalled platform as fine. If only dag_processor is unhealthy, new or edited DAG files will not appear even though existing runs continue.

worked_examples.title: Stop, resume and compare saved history
worked_examples.code:
cd work/airflow
bash run.sh readback
bash run.sh stop
bash run.sh resume
bash run.sh health
bash run.sh readback
worked_examples.interpretation: In an owned workshop, the two readback documents should list the same outputs and saved_observations, because stop and resume keep the container and its PostgreSQL metadata volume. Readback only inspects files and metadata, so running it twice must not create new runs. If the second readback shows fewer summaries, something deleted state between the calls; check whether down or destroy was run instead of stop, and read bash run.sh logs before starting anything new.

worked_examples.title: Separate waiting work from failed work
worked_examples.code:
cd work/airflow
bash run.sh status
bash run.sh logs
bash run.sh health
worked_examples.interpretation: Status shows whether the airflow container is running and healthy, the bounded logs show the last 100 lines, and health names which component is unhealthy. A task stuck in queued with a healthy scheduler usually points to pool or concurrency limits, while a task that never leaves scheduled with an unhealthy scheduler points to the scheduler process itself. A failed task has a log with an exception and a retry count; treat that as an application problem and fix its inputs, not the platform.

evidence: Project-only actual product commands with independent fixture oracles. Source preparation, native runtime observations and restart evidence are recorded separately in the workshop qualification ledger.
